## VIC column closure: a mirror ghost folded into the end blocks (`Bnd`) {#sec-ch07-vic-closure}

### Summary

The system of @eq-ch07-vic-blocks reaches one cell beyond each end of the column. The VIC takes the increment
there to be the reflection of its neighbour's. That is a closed wall: no mass, transverse momentum or energy
crosses it, and the normal momentum keeps the wall pressure.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Closes the column system at its bottom and top, and next to solid cells, by treating the unknown ghost
increment as the mirror of the first interior one; @eq-ch07-vic-closure.
**Data.** In: the first and last interior increments $\boldsymbol\delta_0$, $\boldsymbol\delta_{n-1}$ of each column
[units of $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$ in the solved variables, total density $\rho$ first] and the mirror $\mathrm{Bnd}=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,1,1,1)$ [-];
next to a solid, the solid flag of the neighbour. Out: the ghost increments $\boldsymbol\delta_{-1}$,
$\boldsymbol\delta_n$ folded into the first and last rows, same units. Check cases: an 8-layer moving column with
mirror ghosts, zero gravity.
**Placement.** Inside the sweep, in the first and last rows.
**Activation.** None; fixed by the kernel, whatever the boundary condition of the explicit stage.
**Guarantee / limits.** A reflecting closure in every case.
**Evidence.** No dedicated ctest: the closure runs in every VIC column test, so its own tolerance is **missing
evidence**. Check: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_closure_check.py`, output `vic_closure_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C4]`, tolerance per claim stated in each line; committed output: all 4 PASS; the check ports the code at the pin.
:::

### Derivation

With $\mathrm{Bnd} = \mathrm{diag}(1,-1,1,1,1)$ (or $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,1)$ for the partial system), setting
$\boldsymbol\delta_{-1} = \mathrm{Bnd}\,\boldsymbol\delta_0$ in the first row and $\boldsymbol\delta_n = \mathrm{Bnd}\,\boldsymbol\delta_{n-1}$ in the last
gives

$$
a_0 \leftarrow a_0 + b_0\,\mathrm{Bnd}, \quad a_{n-1} \leftarrow a_{n-1} + c_{n-1}\,\mathrm{Bnd} .
$$ {#eq-ch07-vic-closure}

This equals solving with the ghosts kept and eliminated, to $7\times10^{-15}$ relative [check
`src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_closure_check.py`, output `vic_closure_check.out`, `[C1]`]. When the ghost state is the
mirror of the edge cell, the Roe state at the wall has zero normal velocity (`[C4]`). The flux Jacobian then
satisfies $J_g\,\mathrm{Bnd} = -\mathrm{Bnd}\,J_0$, so the linearised wall flux of every row with
$\mathrm{Bnd} = +1$ cancels. On a moving, layered Cartesian column, the column sums of the mass, transverse
momentum and energy rows of the closed operator vanish to $2\times10^{-16}$. The normal momentum row keeps an
order-one wall term (`[C2]`). Without the closure the column loses mass through its ends (`[C3]`).

In the code, @eq-ch07-vic-closure is the closure with `Bnd` ({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}).

See @fig-ch07-vic-closure for the bottom end.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-vic-closure
#| fig-cap: "The bottom of a column. The ghost increment (purple, dashed) is the mirror $\\mathrm{Bnd}\\,\\boldsymbol\\delta_0$ of the first cell's, $\\mathrm{Bnd}=\\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,1,1,1)$, so its coupling $b_0\\boldsymbol\\delta_{-1}$ folds into the diagonal block as in @eq-ch07-vic-closure. The top is the same with $c_{n-1}$."
#| fig-alt: "A dashed purple ghost cell left of a thick wall line and two interior cells to its right, with an arrow from the first cell to the ghost and the closure formula beside them."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.fig_vic_closure import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The full kernel sets `Bnd` with $-1$ on the normal momentum ({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}). It
adds the closure at the first and last cell of the column and next to a solid cell, unless the block is not the
first or last in $x_1$ or the direction is periodic. The dispatch always passes `periodic` as false
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}). The partial kernel does the same with its 3 x 3 `Bnd`
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_partial_impl.h vic_assemble_partial_impl >}}). The blocks next to a solid cell use a mirror of the fluid
cell instead of the solid's state, so the solid acts as a wall from inside the column, through `solid_lower`
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The implicit closure is always a reflecting wall. A column whose explicit boundary is open, or an outflow,
still has a closed wall in its implicit solve.
:::

1. **Mismatch with the explicit boundary.** The assembled end blocks use the ghost states the explicit boundary
   condition filled. Only for a reflecting boundary are those the mirror the closure assumes.
2. **No periodic $x_1$.** The periodic branch is unreachable, since the dispatch passes false.
3. **No dedicated test.** No ctest checks the closure on its own.
